User Roles and Permissions in MongoDB 
========================================== 
| User 
| Role 
 
 
| Responsibility 
| ----- 
| --------- 
 
 
| --------------------- 
| Ravi 
| read 
 
 
| Can only view student records 
| Sita 
| readWrite 
 
 
| Can view and modify student records 
| Kiran 
| dbAdmin 
 
 
| Can create indexes and manage collections but 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
not insert student data 
| Admin 
| userAdmin 
 
 
| Can create/delete users 
 
Create a Super Admin (All Permissions) 
======================================================= 
Switch to the admin database: 
use admin 
 
Create the root user: 
 
db.createUser({ 
 user: "superadmin", 
 pwd: "admin123", 
 roles: [ 
 { role: "root", db: "admin" } 
 ] 
})

chunks.text:
If you want a user to have: Read data, Insert, Update, Delete data, Administrative privileges (indexes, 
collections, statistics) then assign both readWrite and dbAdmin roles. 
Example 
Login as admin 
mongosh -u superadmin -p admin123 --authenticationDatabase admin 
 
use college 
 
db.createUser({ 
 user: "faculty", 
 pwd: "faculty123", 
 roles: [ 
 { role: "readWrite", db: "college" }, 
 { role: "dbAdmin", db: "college" } 
 ] 
}) 
 
exit 
 
Login 
mongosh -u faculty -p faculty123 --authenticationDatabase college 
 
use college 
Read 
db.students.find() 
Insert 
db.students.insertOne({ 
 rollNo:5, 
 name:"Ramesh" 
})

If you also want the user to create other users 
Then include the userAdmin role as well: 
 
use college 
 
db.createUser({ 
 user: "admin", 
 pwd: "admin123", 
 roles: [ 
 { role: "readWrite", db: "college" }, 
 { role: "dbAdmin", db: "college" }, 
 { role: "userAdmin", db: "college" } 
 ] 
})
